claim: Figure 25 (patterns): the manual's animation section (p. 11, with the pattern drawings in Appendix A) says there are 24 patterns in two banks of 12, one bank for BASS and one for MIDS, and that patterns 1 and 13 are fixed without animation and cannot be edited. MusicRadar confirms 12 patterns per frequency type. Sound on Sound (original MuRF) says the first pattern of each of its two banks is static. Premier Guitar says '1 and 12' are fixed, which conflicts on the second number (and contradicts itself on the same page).

claim: Figure 26 (stereo): the manual section 'Using Both Audio Outputs Together' (pp. 14-15) says that with only LEFT/MONO connected all eight filters are summed to that jack, and that adding RIGHT sends odd-numbered filters to Left and even-numbered filters to Right. 'Audio Path' in Technical Information (p. 28) says that in bypass the dry signal appears only at LEFT/MONO and nothing at RIGHT. MusicRadar independently confirms the odd-left/even-right split; no non-Moog source was found for the mono-summing or bypass statements (Sound on Sound confirms the odd/even split for the original MuRF only).
checks: stereo: odd-numbered filters go to the Left/Mono output and even-numbered filters to the Right output; with only Left/Mono connected all eight are summed there; in bypass the signal appears only at Left/Mono

claim: Figure 29 (ENVELOPE): the manual (p. 12, Figure 11 on p. 13) says the control morphs the envelope shape and describes: 0 choppy because the decay is shortened; around 2 a sharp attack with a quick smooth decay (the basic setting); around 5 smooth and tremolo-like with equal attack and decay; around 6 swirly, with attack and decay long enough for filters to crossfade; around 8 'backwards', with a fast smooth attack and abrupt decay. The text read gave no description of the top (10) setting; the only mention of '10' is in the expression-pedal section (p. 15) and concerns pedal travel. Independent reviews describe the knob differently: MusicRadar puts even attack and decay at 12 o'clock, Premier Guitar puts sharp attack with smooth decay at 12 o'clock, and the Sound on Sound review (original MuRF) describes inverted blips at the far end, which may not apply to the MIDI MuRF.
checks: what the manual says the ENVELOPE control does at its settings (which shapes at the low end, around 2, at the middle, around 6, around 8 and at the top)
